ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two light springs with stiffness coefficients both k and original lengths both L have one end fixed at two points on a horizontal ceiling separated by 2L, and the other ends jointly connected to an object of mass m. At equilibrium, the angle between the springs and the vertical direction is $37^{\circ}$. If the mass of the object is changed to M, and at equilibrium the angle between the springs and the vertical direction is $53^{\circ}$ ($\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$), then M/m is equal to (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, two light springs with stiffness coefficients both k and original lengths both L have one end fixed at two points on a horizontal ceiling separated by 2L, and the other ends jointly connected to an object of mass m. At equilibrium, the angle between the springs and the vertical direction is 37^{\circ}. If the mass of the object is changed to M, and at equilibrium the angle between the springs and the vertical direction is 53^{\circ} (\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6), find the value of M/m.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two equilibrium states. In the left figure, the upper ends of two identical light springs are fixed at two points on the same horizontal ceiling, the horizontal distance between the two fixed points is marked as 2L, and the lower ends are jointly connected to an object of mass m; the angle between the springs and the vertical dashed-line direction is marked as 37°. The right figure has the same structure, the distance between the two fixed points is still 2L, and the lower ends are connected to an object of mass M; the angle between the springs and the vertical direction is marked as 53°. Then reason: Since the two springs are identical and symmetric, the object is located on the perpendicular bisector of the two fixed points, so the horizontal projection of each spring is L. Let the angle between a spring and the vertical direction be θ, and the spring length be l, then l sinθ = L, therefore l = L/sinθ. The original length of the spring is L, so the elongation Δl = l - L = L(1/sinθ - 1). The magnitude of the elastic force of each spring T = kΔl = kL(1/sinθ - 1). When in equilibrium in the vertical direction, the weight equals the sum of the vertical components of the elastic forces of the two springs: W = 2T cosθ = 2kL(1/sinθ - 1)cosθ. For mass m, mg = 2kL(1/sin37° - 1)cos37°. Given sin37° = 0.6, so cos37° = 0.8. For mass M, Mg = 2kL(1/sin53° - 1)cos53°. Because 53° = 90° - 37°, sin53° = 0.8, cos53° = 0.6. Therefore M/m = [(1/sin53° - 1)cos53°] / [(1/sin37° - 1)cos37°] = [(1/0.8 - 1)×0.6] / [(1/0.6 - 1)×0.8] = [(0.25)×0.6] / [(2/3)×0.8] = (3/20)/(8/15) = 9/32. Final answer: 9/32
